features.name: agy review commands confined to the repo
features.description: Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-agy-review-paths-design.md. The nine prefix rules (cat, head, tail, grep, ls, wc, git status/rev-parse/merge-base) took any argument and any pipe: cat /etc/hosts, git diff -O /etc/hosts and git status | cat /etc/hosts ran live. AGY_REVIEW_ALLOW is now two command(regex:...) rules: no argument may start with /, ~ or = (zsh expands =ls to /bin/ls), have a .. path part or hold a glob; a quoted one may not start with - or contain ..; git ranges (HEAD~1..HEAD, main...HEAD) still pass. allow-agy removes the rules it retired (the prefix rules and older shapes of its own regex rules) and keeps the user's other rules.
acceptance_criteria: outside reads by absolute, home, =name, .. and glob paths are refused, quoted or not, in pipes too
ordinary review commands inside the repo and git ranges still run
allow-agy removes its retired rules and keeps the user's own
live agy run refuses the outside reads and runs the ordinary commands
all 11 harness gates pass
features.evidence: Tests first: test_agy_review_commands_stay_inside_the_repo, test_agy_review_note_names_every_allowed_command and test_allow_agy_removes_the_rules_it_retired failed on the old rules; 209 passed, 1 skipped after. Mutations (leading / allowed, .. part allowed, retired rules kept) each fail a test. Live agy 1.4.3: 6 ordinary commands ran, 12 outside reads refused (cat /etc/hosts, cat '/etc/hosts', ls .., ls ~, ls .*, grep -c localhost /etc/hosts, git diff -O /etc/hosts, git status | cat /etc/hosts, git log -- /etc, head -c 20 =ls, git diff --stat =ls =cat, cat ../agytest/a.txt). Live allow-agy: 10 rules removed, 2 added, mode 600 kept. Two subagent reviews (security, correctness) both found zsh =name expansion (cat =ls read /bin/ls); fixed with a failing test. Correctness review also found the note misdescribing quoted arguments and allow-agy removing a user's own command(regex:^git (fetch|pull)$); both fixed, the latter with a failing test. No re-review: the fixes removed a character and narrowed three prefixes. Symlinks: none tracked point outside in the three repos; untracked pack-skill links point to skill folders. Refused now that ran before: grep long options (--include=), globs, quoted patterns with .. or a backslash. Same round: certifi 2026.10.19 for PYSEC-2026-4320 (4325a9c).

features.name: secret-scan scans only what git would commit
features.description: Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-secret-scan-commit-scope-design.md. The shared Stop hook ran gitleaks --no-git over the whole tree, gitignored build output included: in Handy the 11 GB src-tauri/target/ took 151 s and warned on .rmeta files. The hook now copies the files git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard lists (regular files, no symlinks) into a mktemp folder and scans that with --source ., so .gitleaksignore file:rule:line entries still match; the repo's .gitleaksignore and .gitleaks.toml are passed by path. A file the copy cannot read no longer ends the hook before gitleaks runs: the rest is scanned and the gap blocks (exit 2); with no temp folder the tree is scanned in place. Same logic in the hangar and atelier copies.
acceptance_criteria: a token only in a gitignored file does not warn; tracked and untracked-not-ignored tokens do
a .gitleaksignore file:rule:line entry still suppresses its finding
an unreadable file does not stop the scan and blocks with a warning
Handy Stop scan finishes in about a second with no findings
hangar and atelier copies differ from the template only in the config block
all harness gates pass
features.evidence: Tests first: the stub test (only commit-scope files reach gitleaks) and the gitignored-token case failed on the old hook; the unreadable-file case failed (rc=1) after the first fix; the mktemp-failure case failed (rc=1) after the second. 51 passed after; hangar test-hooks 25 and atelier 27 passed, both init.sh pass; shellcheck clean; harness-verify all gates passed. Handy: 151 s with findings in target/ before, 1.2 s and OK after. Odd names (space, newline, -C, --exclude=*) checked with bsdtar 3.5.3 and GNU tar 1.35 by the reviewers. Two subagent reviews (correctness, security) both found the same fail-open: a tar error under set -e ended the hook with exit 1 before gitleaks ran; fixed with a failing test. A re-review found the same for mktemp/mkdir; fixed with a failing test (fallback to the in-place scan). No third review: that fix is a fallback to the old command, covered by its test. Not changed: harness/guards/secret-scan.sh (this repo's own whole-tree gate) keeps the --no-git walk; flagged as a follow-up.

features.name: handover scripts follow a checked contract
features.description: Owner-run handover scripts live in the repo and a checker requires a log file, no typed secret (-K), a recorded rollback run and resumable steps. Found 2026-10-23: hangar's finish script took four runs.
acceptance_criteria: a script with -K, no log or no recorded rollback is blocked; a compliant one passes

features.name: a cleanup step names its root cause
features.description: A step that deletes or restarts things to clear a symptom must point to its root cause (feat, issue or PROGRESS entry). Found 2026-10-23: 'delete dead pods' hid hangar's graceful-shutdown bug.
acceptance_criteria: a cleanup step without a cause reference is flagged

features.name: failed gates print a diagnosis

acceptance_criteria: a failing check prints reason and message per object; hangar H-001 uses it

acceptance_criteria: preflight in ~/projects names hangar and atelier; inside a repo it prints nothing extra

features.evidence: Tests first: 3 preflight and 1 global-hook assertions failed before the change. preflight.sh now prints a WARN naming each target-repos.txt path under a non-repo working folder; global-hook.sh no longer skips start in such a folder. 25 and 20 tests passed after; run from ~/projects it names hangar and atelier. features.description: Host audit 2026-10-23: 11 of 15 ~/.kiro/prompts files pointed at ~/.kiro/skills/<group>/SKILL.md for groups feat-090 moved into per-repo packs, so /audit, /jira, /intake and others read a missing file. install.sh now copies a prompt only when every SKILL.md it names exists after store-packs, and removes a stale copy of one that does not.
acceptance_criteria: a prompt whose SKILL.md is missing is not installed, and an old copy is removed
a prompt whose SKILL.md exists, or that names none, is installed
on this host every ~/.kiro/prompts file points at an existing SKILL.md after install.sh
features.evidence: Tests first: the missing-skill and skipped-output cases failed on the old install_kiro_prompts; 9 checks pass after, also under /bin/bash 3.2. install.sh now calls it after store-packs. On this host install.sh printed 4 files installed and the 11 pack prompts skipped; every ~/.kiro/prompts file now names an existing SKILL.md, and the 4 kept files match the repo source byte for byte. Two subagent reviews (correctness, security): no confirmed defects; both noted that writing through $(...) rewrote trailing newlines, reverted to the direct sed redirect (no new logic, no re-review). harness-verify all gates passed.
